text: A hypothesis is ‘There will be no difference between how quickly men and women blink in response
to a flash of light’.
Name this type of hypothesis.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Outline one difference between a questionnaire and an interview.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Explain one advantage of collecting data using questionnaires compared to interviews.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text: Explain one weakness of using questionnaires in this study.

text: In the study by Laney et al. (false memory), questionnaires were used to collect data.
The research by Saavedra and Silverman (button phobia) was a case study. It used a variety of
techniques including interviews and a scale (the feelings thermometer).
Suggest one strength of using a variety of techniques in a case study.
Describe what is meant by the research methods of correlations and experiments, using any
examples.
Section B
Answer all questions in this section.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Suggest a quantitative measure of ‘feeling relaxed’ that could be used in this study.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Gregor thinks that variables other than where a person works could influence their feelings
and he is therefore using a matched pairs design.

parts.label: (i)
parts.text: Suggest two variables that would be relevant for matching participants in this study.

parts.label: (ii)
parts.text:
Explain why each of the two variables that you suggested in (b)(i) would be relevant in
this study.

text: Gregor is planning an experiment to compare the feelings of adults who work indoors with the
feelings of adults who work outdoors. He thinks that where a person works may influence how
relaxed they feel at work.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Elise has some ethical concerns.

parts.label: (i)
parts.text:
Some parents could feel that questions about what they eat every day are too personal.
Explain which ethical guideline Elise is concerned about here.

parts.label: (ii)
parts.text:
When children answer questions about food they do not like, it could make them feel
upset about their food preferences.
Explain which ethical guideline Elise is concerned about here.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Elise has decided to use volunteer sampling.

parts.label: (i)
parts.text: Explain how Elise could use volunteer sampling in her study.

parts.label: (ii)
parts.text:
A friend suggests that Elise should use random sampling instead of volunteer sampling.
Suggest one advantage of using random sampling instead of volunteer sampling in
Elise’s study.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
Elise believes that learning is the only factor affecting the children’s food preferences.
Suggest why Elise’s belief could lower the validity of her study.

text: Elise is investigating whether children learn food preferences from their parents. She is conducting
a self-report study to compare the food preferences of children and their parents.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Outline how Samir could operationalise the action ‘jump’ in his study.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Samir’s friend Daniel says the action of ‘jump’ is too similar to ‘hop’. His advice is that Samir
should use the action of ‘nod’ (moving the head up and down) instead of ‘hop’.
Explain why the study would be better if Samir follows Daniel’s advice.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
Samir decides that he needs to video the parrot’s responses so that he can score each
response twice.
Suggest why Samir made this decision.

Section C
Answer all questions in this section.

text: Samir is comparing a parrot’s learning of colour words and action words. His parrot is learning
four colour words (red, blue, yellow, green) and must choose a box of the same colour to receive
a food reward. The parrot is also learning four action words (hop, peck, jump, squawk) and must
perform the correct action to receive a food reward.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Describe how Wyatt could conduct a study using an overt observation to investigate phone
snubbing in men and women.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Identify one practical weakness/limitation with the procedure you have described in your
answer to part (a) and suggest how your study might be done differently to overcome the
problem.
Do not refer to ethics or sampling in your answer.

text: When a person pays more attention to their mobile phone than the person they are with, this is
called ‘phone snubbing’. Wyatt wants to investigate phone snubbing in men and women using an
overt observation.
